parsed.why: Decriminalised 2022 with no documented trans-specific policing or border targeting. Offsetting this: a 2018 attack ended in impunity, employment law excludes trans workers, official and religious hostility, and no recognition of same-sex unions. Single-incident evidence is dated.

A 2024 law bans gender-different entries and transition care, and bars Pride and rainbow displays. Police hostility, organised violence against Pride, a trans killing after passage, and unenforced hate-crime law compound this into organised state-tolerated hostility.

Courts decriminalised conduct in 2024, and Pride marches and a drop-in centre operate openly. Gaps: no gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination protection, non-implementation of partner-recognition rulings, and a December 2024 act blocking foreign same-sex marriage recognition.

Documented state-directed targeting: police raids on a trans-frequented bar with forced undressing and extortion. Also a 2024 campaign with 45 assaults in two months, inadequate police response, and a presidential pledge against homosexuality. No trans-specific protections.

No criminalisation since 1791, but no gender-identity protections and a non-functioning judiciary. Hostility toward visible LGBTI people is documented, especially in the capital. A 2019 death is unresolved, earthquake-camp harassment of trans people is documented, and the record is dated.
